newsitem.title: GERMANY: German group says European bankruptcies up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: German group says European bankruptcies up in 1996.

text.p: The number of bankruptcies in Europe rose last year, breaking a two-year decline as Germany was mainly responsible for the increase, a German credit association said on Thursday.
The Wirtschaftsauskunftei Creditreform said 206,700 companies and private individuals filed for bankruptcy last year, about 3,100 cases more than in 1995.
But the association said the negative trend should stop in 1997 and not reach the record set in 1993 with 220,300 cases.
Germany accounted for 33,000 insolvencies last year, up from 26,500 in 1995, which cost about 500,000 jobs, the association said.
